questions.stem: Why does the anode get smaller during electroplating?

options.text: The anode dissolves in the acid electrolyte
Metal atoms at the anode lose electrons and dissolve into the solution as ions
The anode reacts with oxygen in the air
The electric current melts the anode

questions.explanation: During electroplating, the anode is made of the plating metal. At the anode, metal atoms lose electrons and become metal ions that dissolve into the solution (e.g., Ag → Ag⁺ + e⁻). This replaces the ions being deposited at the cathode and keeps the electrolyte concentration approximately constant.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a reason for electroplating an object?

options.text: To use a cheap metal underneath an expensive metal coating

questions.explanation: Electroplating is used to improve appearance, protect against corrosion, provide a harder surface, and save costs by using a cheap base metal with a thin expensive metal coating. However, electroplating adds a layer of metal to the object, so it does not make the object lighter.
